analysis.title: First Read: NVIDIA Corp - Board of Directors Reinstates Jensen; Our Thoughts
key_insights: NVDA announced Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO on 23 Nov 2026. UBS calls it a clear positive and says it supports its decision to keep the Buy rating and not downgrade.
His departure had created uncertainty around financing, supply-chain strategy and talent retention. UBS expects these concerns to recede.
The land powered shell issue persists, especially if President Trump follows through on Friday comments dissuading companies from building data centers outside the US.
UBS expects NVDA's management structure may become more hierarchical to enable clearer succession plans.
NVDA could pull back on ecosystem financing, but with ~$390B of supply commitments it likely needs to keep the flywheel running to stimulate demand offtake.
US intelligence links between Megaspeed and Chinese intelligence could prompt more hawkish export controls, such as new Commerce Entity List additions or passage of the MATCH Act.
UBS says MATCH could have broader negative implications across tech hardware by creating 'matched set' issues similar to the COVID period.
Focus for NVDA should shift back to execution, the product roadmap and the broader AI opportunity.
Rating Buy, PT $220 unchanged, based on ~12x C2028E P/E applied to C2028E EPS of $18.80. Stock at $169.27 implies 30.7% forecast total return.
UBS estimates have EPS (UBS, diluted) of $17.82 for FY 01/28E vs consensus $16.78, and $18.80 for 01/29E vs consensus $21.78.
The Quantitative Research Review shows no catalyst over the next three months, with industry structure and regulatory environment both rated 3 (no change).

market_movers.rationale: Jensen Huang's reinstatement removes financing, supply-chain and talent uncertainty. PT unchanged at ~12x C2028E EPS of $18.80.

sector_views.rationale: Export-control risk, the MATCH Act and restrictions on overseas data centers are the main industry read-throughs. The MATCH Act could hit the broader tech hardware sector.

earnings_insights: UBS FY 01/28E EPS (UBS, diluted) $17.82 vs consensus estimate $16.78. FY 01/29E UBS estimate $18.80 vs consensus estimate $21.78.

FY 01/27E UBS EPS estimate $9.71 vs consensus estimate $9.65. Q4E UBS estimate $2.94 vs consensus estimate $2.88. Q1 to Q3 of FY 01/27 are shown at $1.87, $2.22 and $2.68 (reported, UBS and consensus equal).
UBS revenue estimates: $427.2B FY 01/27E and $770.7B FY 01/28E (forecast).
risk_factors: Export control tightening via Entity List additions or the MATCH Act.
Restrictions on data centers built outside the US.
NVDA ~$390B supply commitments require continued demand stimulation and ecosystem financing.
Competition from AMD and Intel, and semiconductor cyclicality.
geopolitical: President Trump's Friday comments dissuading companies from building data centers outside the US.
US intelligence established connections between Megaspeed and Chinese intelligence, which could drive hawkish export control actions.
Possible additions to the US Department of Commerce Entity List or passage of the MATCH Act.

tension_points.bull_case: With Huang back, financing, supply-chain and talent uncertainty recedes and focus returns to execution and the AI roadmap.
tension_points.bear_case: The company could pull back on ecosystem financing, yet ~$390B of supply commitments means it must keep the flywheel running. Export controls and the MATCH Act add industry risk.

theme_stances.key_argument: Huang's return is a clear positive that reduces financing, supply-chain and talent uncertainty, so focus returns to execution.
theme_stances.evidence: a clear positive and consistent with our view that the story was not necessarily over
